title: pseudotsuga mucronata var. suberosa
intro: Pseudotsuga mucronata var. suberosa, commonly known as the Paperbark Pine, is a variant of the Paperbark Fir (Pseudotsuga menziesii var. glauca), a plant species in the pine family. It has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties, which can help alleviate respiratory issues such as bronchitis and asthma. The therapeutic actions of Pseudotsuga mucronata var. suberosa include expectorant and mucolytic effects, making it useful in treating coughs and congestion. The bioactive constituents of this plant include terpenoids, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
